_comment: GW5A-25A chipdb-completeness overlay v7. 102/141 target_delta_16dq bits attributed via per-target-bit signature matching across 234 Gowin micro-corpus builds (OBUF/IBUF/IOBUF/TBUF single+16-bit-bus, IODELAY, IDDR/IDDRC, IDES4/8/10/16, OSER4/8/10/16, ODDR/ODDRC, TLVDS, PLLA combos). Each overlay entry fires when an IOLOGIC-EMPTY cell's predicate matches. DQ[12] (tile R36C3, ttyp 247) is 100% covered: all 21 Gowin-only bits are extraction-reachable (8 via these overlay entries, 13 via chipdb IOLOGIC feature codes emitted by set_empty_ioreg_attrs). The 39 remaining invisible bits are truly absent from apicula's GW5A-25A chipdb and do NOT affect DQ[12] — see invisible_bit_explanation.
status: EXTRACTED-AND-VERIFIED, DORMANT. The apicula encoder side is complete (this overlay + set_empty_ioreg_attrs + codex IODELAY patch 834622f). No current nextpnr trigger emits IOLOGICI/IOLOGICO_EMPTY+HAS_REG for SDRAM-DQ, so the overlay is dormant — EXP_HH OSS still builds byte-identical at md5 2eb1dd7b. Closing DQ[12] needs a nextpnr placer trigger (pack the DQ capture FF into IOB IOLOGIC), which is a nextpnr change, not chipdb work.
invisible_bit_explanation: 39 target_delta_16dq bits remain invisible. classify_invisible_v3.py confirmed all 39 have NO chipdb entry (shortval/longval/longfuses) in their own tile-type (ttyp 245/247/396/401) — they are genuinely undocumented in apicula's GW5A-25A chipdb. The corpus-diff method (234 Gowin builds) cannot reach them: there is no chipdb entry to trigger. Reaching them would need perturbative .fs bit-flip RE. Crucially, NONE of the 39 fall in DQ[12]'s 21 Gowin-only bits — DQ[12] extraction is complete. The 39 are parked as a known chipdb-completeness limitation.
